name: gradient-ascii

frames.best_why: The arc is fully lit with a white crest and deep blue body, and the character texture is clearest across it.

tagline: A glowing blue horizon drawn entirely from tiny characters.
summary: A soft blue aurora arc on black, rendered completely in monospaced ASCII glyphs that shimmer and re-sort. The pointer scrambles characters as it passes, and a click throws a wave of them across the glow.
appearance: A broad luminous arc spans the frame, white-hot along its crown and sinking into deep navy below, built from closely packed monospaced characters. Outside the arc the stage falls to solid black, leaving the glow as a band of text-like light.
behaviour: The arc brightens up from black while its light drifts and flickers, the glyphs twinkling and changing. Moving the cursor over it scrambles nearby characters into random signs, and a click sends a ring of them outward before it settles.
use_when: A techy atmospheric backdrop for a developer tool, launch page or terminal-themed hero.
avoid_when: The bright arc fights any text laid over it, and the shader is heavy for a purely decorative layer.
customise: Choose a shape, colour palette, character set, cell size, density, glyph opacity, glow, softness, flow, speed and grain. Scramble radius, click effect, intro and light mode are props.
weight_why: Full-screen field and glyph passes plus a multi-step halo blur run every frame.

a11y.note: The canvas is hidden as decoration and the wrapper is unnamed; the scramble reaction is pointer only.

issues: The first frame is almost black, so the arc only shows up partway through the clip.
The brightest crest blows out to white, losing the character texture there.
polish_why: Distinctive ASCII glow with a rich palette; the blown-out crest loses the character detail.
